item.title: New Zealand's knife-edge parliamentary election delivers no clear winner
item.description: No clear winner was produced in New Zealand’s legislative elections Saturday, setting up the two main blocs – Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's right-wing coalition and opposition leader Chris Hipkins' left-wing alliance – for weeks of political wrangling to attempt to cobble together a majority. Hipkins said that while New Zealanders had spoken, "it may take us a little bit longer to figure out exactly what it is that you've said". Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Cold blast brings springtime snow to alpine regions as temperatures plummet across Australia’s south-east
item.description: Thredbo, Perisher and Mount Hotham all recorded falls, along with Kunanyi/Mount Wellington in Tasmania Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Snow blanketed parts of New South Wales, Victoria and Tasmania across the weekend as an unseasonal cold blast whipped through Australia’s south-east, but forecasters say warm temperatures and thunderstorms are on the way. Thredbo, Perisher and Mount Hotham all recorded falls on Saturday and Sunday, while snow also fell on Kunanyi/Mount Wellington in Hobart. Continue reading... item.title: Victoria Barracks in Sydney and Melbourne to remain in public hands after partial backtrack on defence property selloff
item.description: Four heritage-listed defence properties to be preserved for community use after backlash from veterans and former PMs Get our daily political email , free app or daily news podcast Four heritage-listed defence sites, including Sydney’s Victoria Barracks, will remain in public hands after the Albanese government yielded to public backlash against their sale. The sites, along with 63 others around the country, were identified in an independent audit as being underutilised by defence, not fit for purpose and costly to maintain, and were earmarked for sale to recoup $3bn in the federal budget… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
